Yes. NovaLearn should keep the Advanced OCR Pipeline funded and prioritized ahead of accelerating the Microsoft Teams integration.

- **Current support demand:** Scanned PDF processing is the primary driver of citation errors and onboarding delays, and the Advanced OCR Pipeline scheduled for August 2026 is the highest technical priority [NL-001#NL-001-S08]. The support queue is already overloaded: 27% of May support tickets were related to import issues and broken citations from scanned PDFs [NL-015#NL-015-S06]. The OCR work is a critical system stability requirement, not a nice-to-have [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

- **Onboarding impact:** Scanned PDFs and permission mapping remain the primary onboarding bottleneck [NL-016#NL-016-S01]. The OCR pipeline will deliver verified, page-specific citations and is the correct fix for the ingestion/citation problem [NL-016#NL-016-S07]. Accelerating Teams before this would risk delivering inaccurate, un-cited answers to a broader audience inside chat [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

- **Roadmap status:** OCR is scheduled for August 2026 [NL-001#NL-001-S08] [NL-015#NL-015-S06]. Teams is still in the design phase for Q4 2026, with development slated for early 2027 [NL-001#NL-001-S08] [NL-015#NL-015-S06] [NL-011#NL-011-S07]. It is not generally available, and internal evidence shows the Teams connector is in very early proof-of-concept form, lacking security controls and tenant isolation [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. A rushed Teams launch would require a complete auth-layer redesign and risks a tenant-isolation breach [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

So even though Teams is a high-demand request [NL-011#NL-011-S07], the support demand, onboarding impact, and roadmap status all support funding OCR first and keeping Teams on the Q4 design / early 2027 development path [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
